news.title: Will anyone topple Infantino? How Fifa president is trying to cling on after World Cup sell-off debacle
news.lede: Fifa president continues to lobby for re-election despite no other candidates coming forward to challenge him. For Gianni Infantino there is no international break. The Fifa president is widely expected to make an appearance at the United Nations general assembly this week in New York, where he will lobby heads of state for their federations’ support as he continues his campaign to be re-elected next year. Infantino has not been idle during the lull since Fifa abandoned its World Cup sell-off plan last month, instead crisscrossing the globe on a private jet provided by Qatar Airways as part of its sponsorship deal with world football’s governing body.

news.title: This college football team just adopted Norway's World Cup Viking Row — keeping the viral tradition alive
news.lede: Norway's Viking Row was one of the most viral fan traditions of the 2026 World Cup. Now, two months later, it has officially made its way into American college football. The University of Minnesota debuted its own version of the synchronized rowing chant at its season opener at Huntington Bank Stadium, with the student section sitting in rows and mimicking the same exaggerated rowing motion that Norwegian fans made famous this summer. Former Gophers linebacker Kamal Martin led the chant before kickoff, keeping one of the World Cup's biggest fan traditions going long after the tournament ended.

news.title: Messi, Ronaldo and Bangladesh’s ASEAN Cup: A longer international break, with plenty to watch
news.lede: Club football is taking a near-three-week pause, but there is no shortage of intrigue on the international stage. For the first time, the September and October FIFA windows have been merged into a single 16-day international period, running from September 21 to October 6. Major European clubs played their last match before the break on September 20 and will return to action on October 10, leaving supporters without club football for almost three weeks. National teams, meanwhile, will pack four matches into the extended window instead of the usual two.

news.title: Italy national football team players: the 34 Mancini picked after a third World Cup miss
news.lede: Roberto Mancini is back as Italy coach and has named 34 players for the Nations League, 11 of whom have never been capped. Here is the full squad, and what the caps column says about where Italy are. Italy will miss a World Cup for the third time running, and the squad Roberto Mancini has named for his first competitive matches back in the job is the first real sign of what he intends to do about it. Thirty-four players were called up for the 2026-27 Nations League games against Belgium, Turkey and France.

news.title: Motivated De Bruyne wants to keep playing for Belgium
news.lede: Sept 22 - Belgium midfielder Kevin De Bruyne will continue to play international football as long as he remains motivated, saying he had not considered quitting the team after the World Cup despite being the last of the country's golden generation. De Bruyne, 35, has won 124 caps since his debut as a teenager in 2010 under Georges Leekens and is lined up to add more appearances as Belgium now have Mark van Bommel in charge. The new era begins against Italy in Rome on Friday, followed by Nations League clashes with France (twice) and Turkey over the next three weeks. In recent weeks, De Bruyne has seen long-time colleague Axel Witsel retire and goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois sit out the Nations League but told reporters on Tuesday he had never considered quitting the national team.

news.title: UEFA Grassroots Week 2026: Getting Europe active through football
news.lede: Running from 23-30 September, UEFA Grassroots Week shines a spotlight on the people, programmes and communities that make football accessible and enjoyable for everyone across Europe. UEFA Grassroots Week showcases the power of grassroots football to unite communities and inspire movement. With the support of our strategic partner Lidl, we are showcasing the beauty of the game and its continued positive impact, from the UEFA Football in Schools programme to the array of grassroots initiatives delivered every day by Europe's national football associations. UEFA Grassroots Week takes place every September alongside the European Commission's Week of Sport, which is designed to inspire activity and healthy lifestyle choices across the continent.
